title: Quinoa
summary: Andean seed prized for complete protein — not a true grain.
origins: Domesticated in the Lake Titicaca basin of the Andes (modern Peru and Bolivia). The Quechua and Aymara peoples called it chisaya mama — "mother of all grains" — though botanically it is a chenopod seed, cousin to spinach and beets.
history: Quinoa sustained high-altitude civilizations for millennia before Spanish colonization disrupted its cultivation in favor of wheat. It nearly vanished as a staple until Bolivian and Peruvian farmers revived export markets in the late 20th century. NASA studied it in the 1980s for closed ecological life-support systems because of its protein profile and low water needs.

timeline.event: NASA evaluates quinoa for space agriculture

teaching: Rinse unless the package says pre-washed — saponins taste soapy.
Use 1:2 quinoa-to-water; simmer covered 15 min, rest 5 min, fluff.
Toast dry quinoa 2 minutes before adding liquid for nuttier flavor.
fun_fact: Quinoa isn't a grain — it's a seed. NASA studied it as a space crop because it's protein-dense and water-efficient.
